name: Combined Oxidative Phosphorylation Defect Type 25
aliases: Combined Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Deficiency Type 25

criteria.description: Presence of multisystemic clinical features consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of combined defects in multiple respiratory chain enzyme complexes in muscle or fibroblast biopsy
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation complexes
Brain MRI showing basal ganglia or brainstem abnormalities supportive of mitochondrial disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multisystemic clinical features plus biochemical evidence of combined respiratory chain defects and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, biochemical, and genetic data due to phenotypic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated blood lactate due to impaired oxidative phosphorylation

common.notes: Generalized muscle weakness and reduced muscle tone
Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Various seizure types including focal and generalized
Dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy due to mitochondrial dysfunction
Poor growth and weight gain in infancy

occasional.notes: Enlarged liver due to mitochondrial dysfunction

searchTerms: endocrine issues including high blood sugar

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Combined deficiency of mitochondrial respiratory chain complexes I, III, and IV in muscle biopsy
Elevated serum creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia hyperintensities and cerebral atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins (e.g., NDUFAF6, COX10)
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions may be present
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology on electron microscopy

distinguishingFeatures: Prominent lactic acidosis with episodic neurological deterioration
Isolated optic neuropathy without multisystem involvement
Rapid vision loss in young adults

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in infancy
Severe lactic acidosis refractory to treatment
Multisystem involvement with cardiomyopathy and neurological decline
references: Rahman S, et al. Mitochondrial disease: clinical features and diagnosis. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2020.
Parikh S, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015.
Orphanet: Combined oxidative phosphorylation defect type 25. ORPHA:447954.
